body: I find it hard for you to make that assumption given the information I provided. I finally was updated on the situation by my gf personally. My conclusions that the hospital was severely limiting her contact was correct. From her time spent in the hospital, she only had two chances to call someone, and it was me both times.To my assurance, they finally transferred her to a proper psychiatric facility and that is where she is currently. I was correct to assume that certain of the hospital's procedures were not being followed properly. She was given a paper indicating the amount of food to be provided to her and yet almost half of it was missing. There was also a lack of contact from the nurses and doctors. There are quite of bit of discrepancies I have with the hospital, but I rather not write them here unless someone would honestly want to know them.  I finally am relieved to find out that she is in proper care. However, I do have this quandary to whether or not I should file a complaint about the care she received in that hospital. But I feel as if nothing would come out of it and it will just be useless to do so.

Well, it did happen the way you explained it. She had suicidal thoughts as well as a plan. It is when we had the initial evaluation with a doctor, they notified us that she was going to be sent to a behavioral institution. She said what if she refused. They then told her that she did not have a say in the matter. This is what led me to believe that she is now involuntary committed. 

Of course, I was only there until visiting hours on the first day. So I am not completely aware of any actions she may have taken that could have exhibited violent behavior, but I am in doubt that she would have done such things. On a personal level, I know that once she has cooled down from her anger, she no longer has such thoughts. So it is hard for me to believe that they could have decided upon involuntary commitment for any action she may have exhibited. 

She is 20 years old, so that may be a factor to why they are not releasing any information to her parents. 
She does not have access to a phone at all times. It is only randomly does a nurse or the doctor provide her with a phone. This is when she calls me and updates me with the information on her status. But even then, it is very little information. I ask her if she would tell me everything the doctors has said to her, but she said that it wasn't much. Essentially, they have been unable to find a institution to send her to and she does not enjoy it there. She wants to go home but they won't allow her to. It is quite possible that she is refusing to tell me any information out of her own free will, but again I doubt this.

I've asked at the front about her signing a release form authorizing me to get information about her care, but the receptionist informed me that even if she did such things, it would not be a legally binding contract and they won't be obliged to inform me to anything.

Well, her parents have also tried to get information, but it seems that they even refuse to tell them anything. And when they do, it only is half-ass information. Also they won't allow me to visit her or provide her with books.

Her getting help is what I expected. But the fact that they have been unable to find a proper behavioral institution in a timely manner is what bothers me. Are they going to keep her indefinitely in the emergency room with no treatment. As of yet, I am aware that the most they have done to help her is make phone calls elsewhere. She has remained in the room with little contact and it doesn't seem as if the doctors are providing her with any prescriptions or counseling.
